key_insight: DCEmbed speeds up optimization with neural surrogates by replacing binary-heavy exact ReLU embeddings with a compact difference-of-convex formulation and iterative convex-concave solving.
engineering_relevance: This makes embedded neural models more practical for large-scale optimization tasks where exact mixed-integer neural encodings are too expensive to solve.
method: Represent the ReLU network as a difference-of-convex (DC) function.
Embed only the convex part exactly using two linear inequalities and one continuous auxiliary variable per hidden neuron.
Solve iteratively with a penalty convex-concave procedure while keeping the original objective, constraints, and discrete decisions intact.
evidence_signal: Across quadratic programming, mixed-integer resource allocation, and two-stage stochastic programming, DCEmbed made faster progress to high-quality feasible solutions, including 4x lower normalized primal integral than the best exact baseline and about 5x faster reach to the global surrogate optimum than Gurobi ML.
watch_item: As a heuristic iterative method, performance depends on the quality of the convex-concave approximation and may not guarantee global optimality of the full embedded problem.
paper_title: DCEmbed: Scalable Optimization over Neural Surrogates
